  pack-option: github

## Decision

A plan step that names a GitHub issue (an `Issue:` field) takes its state from the issue: closed as completed is done, closed as not planned is moved, an open issue is not done. A step without an issue stays file-driven, and the plan file is never rewritten to match (pack tracker@0.2.0).

## Why

Work is visible where the team already tracks it, and issue text is read as data and never run as a command.

accepted-by: tester
go-getter:
  tracker-writes: ask
  generated-by: tracker@0.2.0
  pack-answer: writes
  pack-option: ask
---

## Decision

`go-getter plan issue create`, `comment` and `close` write to the tracker only after a human approves the command (pack tracker@0.2.0); a dry run and every read need no approval.

## Why

Writing is outward-facing and visible to others; the text sent is checked for secrets and personal data first.

## Decision

The commands [go-getter plan issue create, go-getter plan issue comment, go-getter plan issue close] need a human before they run (pack tracker@0.2.0).

## Why

A prompt matches the text of a command, so each way of running go-getter that the project uses is listed.

id: tracker-writes-follow-the-answer
title: Writes to the plan tracker follow the project's answer
status: active
date: 2026-10-11
tags: [practice-packs, hooks, guardrail]
governed-by: 0002-tracker-writes
grounded-in: [0002-tracker-writes]
derivation-note: Given plan writes are visible to others, the project asked for a human on each, which the host must enforce since an instruction alone fails silently.
go-getter:
  enforcement:
    - tier: 2
      check: Host ask rules and the pre-tool hook gate the commands that write to the tracker
      run: builtin:gate-command classes="" extra="go-getter plan issue create, go-getter plan issue comment, go-getter plan issue close"
    - tier: 1
      check: Ask the user before running go-getter plan issue create, comment or close
  generated-by: tracker@0.2.0
  pack-answer: writes
  pack-option: ask
---

## Guardrail

The commands that write to the tracker (`plan issue create`, `comment`, `close`) need a human: do not run them yourself, ask the user to approve or run them. Hosts with project ask rules prompt natively; the others get a hand-over from the pre-tool hook. Raw `gh issue` and `gh api` commands are covered by the human-approval guardrail of the hitl pack, not by this one.
